What it promises

Business rules are conditions the code insists on: what must be true before something runs, what it guarantees afterwards and what is always true. Shown here: the rules that most use cases rely on.

  • Items is always zero or greater.

    Always trueUnknownApplies to CartRelied on by 4 use cases

  • Percent must be zero or greater. Percent must be at most 100.

    ConditionUnknownApplies to rebateRelied on by 3 use cases

  • The result will be zero or greater.

    GuaranteeUnknownApplies to totalRelied on by 3 use cases

  • Qty must be zero or greater.

    ConditionUnknownApplies to totalRelied on by 3 use cases

  • Unit must be zero or greater.

    ConditionUnknownApplies to totalRelied on by 3 use cases

All behaviour changes

How to read this

Use case
Something the software can be asked to do: an entry point of the code.
Business rule
A condition written into the code. It is checked or proved, so it cannot silently stop being true.
Status of a rule
Proved: a verifier showed it always holds. Checked at run time: the program stops when it is broken. Open: nothing enforces it. Unknown: the snapshot does not say.
Capability
A way to reach outside the program: files, network, the clock, other programs, the console. The software has exactly the capabilities listed.
